target_customer: Consumers who want to talk by voice with strangers about shared topics; monetized through app subscriptions (not detailed by a source)
problem: People want real conversation with strangers without the pressure of video or profiles; Wakie started as a wake-up call from a stranger and became a voice chat community.
business_model: Consumer social app (monetization not documented in sources found)

founders.name: Hrachik Ajamian
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder; the company site says he also co-founded SleepDoctor, MedPair and Pearch.

founders.name: Tat Ajamyan
founders.background_notes: Named by the company site as a co-founder and brother of Hrachik; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time voice calling at scale with moderation and matching on mobile is standard but non-trivial for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Value depends on a pool of users to match, but voice chat apps are easy to copy and users move between them.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying or acquisition was found in sources; the app remained independent and later marketed itself as an Omegle alternative after Omegle closed in 2023.

market_need_then: In February 2016 TechCrunch reported Wakie pivoting from alarm calls to talking with a stranger on any subject, quoting the founder that people want human conversation for emotional or controversial topics.

branding.domain_note: Uses wakie.com; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and anti-loneliness, framed as voice-first community

branding.brand_signature: Wake-up call from a stranger concept
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fast Company, Gizmodo, Macworld and The Next Web in 2014 and 2015 for the wake-up-by-stranger idea.

brand_strength.rationale: Early press such as Gizmodo and Fast Company covered the concept, but the name is tied to waking up and the product later moved to general voice chat.

pivots.from: Social alarm clock where a stranger calls to wake you
pivots.to: Voice calls with a stranger on any topic
pivots.why: Founder argued people want human conversation for topics Siri and Google handle poorly (TechCrunch, 2016-02-23)

outcome_analysis: Wakie began in 2014 as a stranger wake-up call app, raised about $1M in August 2014 from Russian funds, joined YC in Winter 2016 and pivoted that February to topic-based voice conversation. It is still active as of 2026 with a community and clubs, but funding data are thin and conflicting at $2M to $4M total, so its commercial scale is unknown.
notes: The 2014 round is stated by Ventureburn and FinSMEs and predates the YC batch. A YC-era seed (Wellfound lists Seed, February 2016, total $2M) and a $69K seed appear only in aggregators, not recorded. Totals range $2M to $4M. Wakie is the international version of the Russian app Budist per press; the brand existed in the US since about 2011 for Russian speakers per a snippet, unverified. No competitor with a source dated near February 2016 was found; Opentalk appears only on an undated AlternativeTo page.
